subject: Field upgrade: offline image rotation procedure and authority handshake

Subject: Re: field upgrade windows for air-gapped clusters

Hi Markus,

Thanks for taking this. We have an upcoming phased update across 12 air-gapped sites in Q3 and need a clear, auditable procedure for accepting and rotating signed images on the appliance fleet. Two specific asks:

- What is Redwood's recommended authority/keys model for signing images for offline installation? We need to map who holds private keys, where signatures are verified, and what the field operator handoff looks like.
- Can you provide a minimal offline checklist for transporting, validating, and applying images (manifest verification, signature checks, and post-install smoke tests)?

We've had divergent practices with other vendors and need one reproducible flow we can run in our compliance audits. Attaching our current offline-transfer checklist for context.

Appreciate a short proposal we can review this week.

Best,
Sara
Head of Ops, DataLock Systems

Subject: Re: field upgrade: offline image rotation procedure and authority handshake

Sara —

Thanks for the checklist. I drafted a concise field procedure and a key custody model that should meet audit requirements while keeping operator steps minimal. Key points here, full manifest attached: image-signing-manifest-v2.yaml

1) Authority model
- Primary signing: Redwood Release Authority (offline HSM, threshold policy). Private keys never leave HSM.
- Delegate signing: For customer-managed images, we support an external signing key blob that Redwood will validate against an accepted CA root.
- Verification: Each appliance includes a vendor-embedded trust root and a signing-root rotation mechanism tied to a signature chain in the manifest.

2) Offline transfer steps (high level)
- Prepare bundle on air-gapped machine -> generate manifest (sha256 checksums + signature references).
- Sign bundle in HSM -> produce .signed wrapper.
- Transfer via verified physical media (USB with tamper seal) to site; operator runs local verifier which checks manifest signature chain then verifies image checksums.
- Apply update in maintenance window; smoke tests run against local health endpoints; results written to signed local log.

3) Emergency rollback
- Keep previous signed image on-site and manifest versioned; rollback controlled via signed rollback token issued by Redwood authority.

Next steps I propose: Laura to confirm KMS/HSM integration and required key artifacts; Rishi to draft operator checklist with exact CLI commands and time estimates; Marissa to coordinate field validation dates with DataLock.

I attached image-signing-manifest-v2.yaml and a signed image sample (signed-image-redwood-v1.signed) for validation.

Markus
Director, Field & Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: image-signing-manifest-v2.yaml; signed-image-redwood-v1.signed

Subject: Re: field upgrade: offline image rotation procedure and authority handshake

Markus/Sara —

Reviewed the manifest and the proposed authority chain. A few clarifications from security/crypto side:

- HSM model: we currently support Azure Key Vault HSM + on-prem Thales Luna for enterprise Private deployments; both support key import with a wrap/unwrap policy. For air-gapped signing we will use an isolated signing station that connects to the HSM in a constrained manner (sign-only account) and produces signatures with a deterministic, audited nonce.
- Signature format: we prefer a compact COSE-raw wrapper; manifest will contain the COSE header and a certificate chain reference. We'll provide a small verifier (single static binary) to run on-site for customers who cannot install the full Redwood runtime.
- Key rotation: recommend a quarterly rotation cadence for root signing keys with a 2-week overlap period during transition. The manifest format supports multiple valid signatures to permit warm rollover.

I'll create the KMS integration doc with the exact commands and sample certificate blobs. Rishi — can you incorporate the verifier binary call and example outputs into your operator checklist?

Laura
Senior Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: field-verifier-instructions.md (to follow)

Team —

I've converted the high-level steps into a runnable operator checklist and timed the windows using our standard verification suite. Highlights:

- Prep & sign stage (off-site): ~45–60 minutes per bundle (includes HSM signing and manifest generation).
- Transfer & verify on-site: ~20 minutes (verify signature chain, checksum, unpack).
- Apply & smoke test: ~30 minutes (service bring-up + lightweight ML self-check).
- Rollback : ~15 minutes to swap to previous image and confirm service is healthy.

Operator checklist (CLI excerpts):
- Verify manifest signature: ./redwood-verifier --verify --manifest image-signing-manifest-v2.yaml --root-roster roots.pem
- Verify image checksums: sha256sum -c image-checksums.txt
- Install: ./redwood-install --apply signed-image-redwood-v1.signed --maintenance-window 00:30
- Post-install tests: curl -fsS localhost:4200/health || exit 1; ./redwood-selftest --ml-check --quick

I attached a plain-text checklist (field-operator-checklist.txt) and a short rollback playbook (field-rollback-playbook.txt). I recommend we pre-stage the verifier binary and signed previous image on each site to reduce risk.

Rishi
Site Reliability Lead, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
